title: WoWShell First Release!  Stages WoW assets in for use in Godot.  Rally Racer, StarCraft2 Demo, WoW Replica and more!
author: AverageDrafter
selftext:
[https://discord.gg/PzQGgzGNrH](https://discord.gg/PzQGgzGNrH)

[https://github.com/AverageDrafter/WoWShell/releases/latest](https://github.com/AverageDrafter/WoWShell/releases/latest)

Download the zip - run the setup and then the bat files for each project - or run them directly from Godot if you want.  The .bat are Godot command lines to run each project, you can look at them to see what they do.

WoWShell is a project I have been working on for months, including three major versions.  The idea is to be able to prototype new games using the World of WoW as your base.  Included are a patched version of Godot (some minor memory and renderer fixes) and the documentation and python scripts to extract and utilize already installed WoW asset data for use in Godot.  
  
WoWShell and the games it makes distributes with no Blizzard Assets, and instead uses the user's current install to either stream the data directly, or convert the data into a Godot/WoWShell friendly format.  This setup process takes about an hour and 20GB of space, but only needs to be run once, and all the games and WoWShell itself pull from this repository.  I intend to get both of those down as much as possible, but for playtesting and the initial release, these are acceptable.

With this initial release the intent is that it will mostly be accessed and utilized by AI - with documentation set up for this purpose.  I will follow feedback on more human friendly documentation, but for now AI assisted is assumed.

There is a lot of work to do on fidelity, but the idea is not to recreate the game World of Warcraft, even with our Replica.  Our goal is to stage all the assets in Godot, as closely as possible to how they are presented in WoW, so that they can then be used to make any number of new games that take as little and as much as they need from the existing structure.

One of the things I was able to add are Seamless Portals for instances.  Or as I kept calling them "Portal-type-Portals"  In the racer video you can the transitions from Dire Maul and Wailing Caverns with this portal mode active.  In DM the lighting changes and the far portal flickers a bit as you transition from Instance to Kalimdor.  As you move from Kalimdor to Wailing Caverns... I don't even notice where the transition is.

No frame skips, no load screens, full visibility through the portal.  20 year old tech comes to a 25 year old game!  You can make a seamless Tram ride from Ironforge to Stormwind.  The other portals are setup but not tested, so you should see... interesting results.  Lots will default to the standard load, especially outdoor ones.  Each are going to take individual work to make flawless.

In addition to the racer, there is the "Replica" - our purposefully incomplete rebuild of WoW.  WoWShell does not attempt to recreate many of the MMO aspects or several of the systems that make WoW the game that it is.  Benilla is a much better project to use for that purpose, as it is a full decompile of the client side - one we used since its release to help use improve our fidelity.

Our is a restaging of the assets in Godot so you have all the benefits of a game engine, physics, shader support, renderer, game structure (loops, signals, timers) but with everything set up, as much as possible, as it is in WoW.

Then you use as much or as little as you need to make the game you want.

The other short demo is the first level of StarCraft2 - Liberation Day.  It is a recreation of the Backwater Station map, with WoW like quests and the SC2 style UI.  It is very rough, the models don't collide for instance.  But mostly it was a test to see if the extraction technique could be used on other Blizzard games in the CASC (the long block data format Blizzard stores its game data in)  
  
It can!

comments.author: NorberAbnott
comments.body: You really think it's feasible to release a game and say "valid World of Warcraft installation is required for you to play my game"? Why does it take an hour to convert the assets rather than making your code load the assets as-is?

replies.author: AverageDrafter
replies.body:
Because there are trade offs to the approach to how you want to do this sort of thing. Benilla requires a you to find a 1.12 client and a then separate 1.12 server.  As do private servers.  
  
WoWShell doesn't require additional downloads if you have WoW classic live installed, and most people who will be interested will.  If you don't have WoW installed, you can get it right from the official source.

The installation is for the full WoW asset package, and is required once.  It take the existing data and converts into a more Godot usable format from the CASC once, for all WoWShell projects.  And my near term goal is to cut how much needs to be reconverted as much as possible, and speed up how we do that.  That takes cycles of implementations and testing I used to improve the game time performance and visuals first.

And the nature of the project means its for prototypes, novelties, fan projects, etc.  "Release" a game under these terms is pretty much give it out for free, and yes its very feasible to do that.

comments.author: Holistictragedy
comments.body: I think wowshell is a cool concept and I fully support you! As soon as I have a PC I will want to fork this! There's great value for the community in what you're building! Keep going, bro!
